bib.title: OCR-Memory: Optical Context Retrieval for Long-Horizon Agent Memory

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "OCR-Memory: Optical Context Retrieval for Long-Horizon Agent Memory", Jinze Li, Yang Zhang, Xin Yang, Jiayi Qu, Jinfeng Xu, Shuo Yang, Junhua Ding, Edith C.-H. Ngai (HKU, UNT, Tsukuba, Yonsei). arXiv 2604.26622v1 [cs.CL], 29 Apr 2026. Preprint (the template looks like an ACL-style submission, but no venue is printed).
COVERAGE: All 47,499 chars read, including Tables 1-7, Limitations, references and Appendix A. Nothing skipped.

FIT WARNING: Partial fit. The paper is about episodic trajectory retrieval under a token budget. It is not about distilled memory, and the only distillation-style baselines (AWM, MemoryBank, ACON) are compared as black boxes. There is no full-context baseline, and tokens are not matched across all methods. It suits a chapter section on "retrieval fidelity and token cost of episodic memory". It does not suit "raw vs distilled memory".

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Claim: OCR-Memory beats all text baselines on Mind2Web and AppWorld at the same default memory-module context of 4096 tokens.
 number: Mind2Web Ele Acc 53.8 vs Retrieval 41.3, AWM 49.1, ACON 48.2; AppWorld avg 58.1 vs Zero-Shot 41.9, Retrieval 46.2, AWM 55.0, ACON 56.2.
 setup: GPT-4 agent (temp 0), Mind2Web Cross-Task split, AppWorld. Single run, no variance reported. The margins over AWM and ACON are 1.9 to 4.7 points.
 quote: "OCR-Memory improves Element Accuracy from 49.1% to 53.8% and increases Step Success Rate to 46.1%, achieving a state-of-the-art Task Success Rate of 4.8%."
 where: Sec 6.2 and Table 1.
2. Claim: Against text RAG, the gap widens as the token budget tightens.
 number: Ele Acc gain +17.0 at 1024 tokens, +14.0 at 2048, +12.5 at 4096, +12.6 at 8192.
 setup: Mind2Web, context budgets 1024 to 8192, Text-RAG vs OCR-Memory. Gains are read off Figure 2's axis labels, and the text only says "the performance gap widens as the token budget becomes more restrictive."
 quote: "OCR-Memory consistently outperforms Retrieval method across all four Mind2Web metrics, and the performance gap widens as the token budget becomes more restrictive."
 where: Sec 6.3 and Fig 2.
3. Claim: Token cost moves from the reasoning context to storage and latency. It is not cheaper on every axis.
 number: Text tokens per step fall from 3,980 to 596 (6.7x). Disk per episode rises from 18 KB to 1.47 MB. Retrieval latency rises from 0.3 s to 1.7 s.
 setup: Mind2Web, continuous logging, Text-RAG vs OCR-Memory. The 596 count is text tokens injected into the reasoning LLM. The visual tokens read by the 3B retriever are counted separately and are not in this figure.
 quote: "OCR-Memory reduces the text tokens injected into the reasoning LLM from 3,980 to 596 per step, a 6.7× reduction, at the cost of increasing disk storage per episode from 18 KB to 1.47 MB and retrieval latency from 0.3 s to 1.7 s."
 where: Table 7, Sec 6.3.
4. Claim: Adaptive resolution (old history at low resolution, upscaled when retrieved) keeps almost all of the accuracy at about a third of the visual tokens.
 number: Step SR 46.1 at 82 tokens per frame, vs 46.5 at 256 (static high-res) and 39.7 at 65 (static low-res).
 setup: Mind2Web. "Avg Tokens" is visual tokens per history frame. The five most recent steps are at 1024x1024 (256 tokens) and the rest at 512x512 (64 tokens).
 quote: "Static Low-Res (5122) 39.7 2.9 65 / Static High-Res (10242) 46.5 4.9 256 / Dynamic (Ours) 46.1 4.8 82"
 where: Table 3.
5. Claim: Letting the model select segment indices and then fetching the stored verbatim text gives a faithful retrieval stage. Free-form generation of the memory text is less faithful and about 3x slower.
 number: Faithfulness 100.0% vs 84.3% for free-form. Ablation: Step SR 46.1 (SoM) vs 39.2 (text generation), latency 1.7 s vs 5.3 s. Retrieval Recall@1 is 78.6 vs 52.7 for dense text RAG.
 setup: Mind2Web. The retrieval subset is built from same-website trajectories, with pseudo-gold steps taken from uncompressed logs. The 100% is by construction, and the authors say so.
 quote: "This faithfulness metric measures whether the recovered text exactly matches stored evidence after a segment has been selected; it does not imply that every selected segment is always relevant."
 where: Tables 2 and 6, Sec 6.3.
6. Claim: Optical compression of text is about 10x, with retrieval accuracy that degrades slowly with length.
 number: Compression 10.3x with 98.5% Recall@1 at 4k tokens, down to 94.1% at 32k (10.6x).
 setup: RULER needle-in-a-haystack, rendered to images, DeepSeek-OCR encoder.
 quote: "maintaining a retrieval accuracy of 98.5% at 4k length and sustaining 94.1% even when the context extends to 32k tokens."
 where: Table 4.
 Minor: Qwen3-32B backbone, Mind2Web, Ele Acc 48.6 vs RAG 35.2 (Table 5).

BASELINES AND TOKEN MATCHING
- Baselines: Zero-Shot (no history), dense-vector text Retrieval (RAG), MemoryBank (Zhong 2024), AWM (Wang 2024, distilled workflows), ACON (Kang 2025, context compression).
- There is no full-context baseline and no raw-trajectory-in-prompt baseline. The paper says full trajectories are impractical.
- Tokens are matched only partly. The text says "same context-budget setting" and "strictly set to 4096 tokens by default" for the memory module. Only Text-RAG is swept across budgets (Fig 2). AWM, ACON and MemoryBank are not swept, and their token use is not reported.
- Table 7 shows the injected text tokens are not equal (3,980 vs 596), so the headline comparison is not token-matched on the reasoning side.
- The OCR-Memory retriever is a trained 3B model (DeepSeek-OCR, LoRA fine-tuned on HotpotQA supporting facts). The baselines get no such training. Retriever compute and its visual tokens are outside the reported token counts.
- Task SR on Mind2Web is very low for every method (2.2 to 4.8), so differences are small in absolute terms.

LIMITS
- Authors concede three costs. It needs a fine-tuned retriever. Rendering is more expensive and uses more disk. The vision encoder adds a memory footprint.
- Not shown: any full-context or oracle upper bound; any cross-task transfer or learning-from-experience test beyond retrieval; variance or seeds; the cost of the AWM and ACON runs; models newer than GPT-4 and Qwen3-32B; a test of whether the image matters. The retriever could in principle be a text cross-encoder trained on the same HotpotQA data, and that comparison is missing. This confounds "optical" with "trained retriever".
- Table 1 is not itself a controlled test of raw vs distilled memory.
- Gains are reported as "state-of-the-art" on only two benchmarks.
- The 6.7x claim is on reasoning-context tokens only.

BUILDS ON
- DeepSeek-OCR (Wei et al., 2025), optical context compression.
- Set-of-Mark prompting (visual anchors).
- MemoryBank (Zhong et al., AAAI 2024).
- Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al., 2024).
- ACON (Kang et al., arXiv 2510.00615, 2025).
- MemGPT (Packer et al., 2023).
- Generative Agents (Park et al., 2023).
- Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023).
- Self-RAG (Asai et al., 2023).
- ExpeL (Zhao et al., AAAI 2024).
- RAPTOR (Sarthi et al., 2024).
- RAG (Lewis et al., 2021).
- LLMLingua (Jiang et al., EMNLP 2023).
- Benchmarks: Mind2Web (Deng et al., NeurIPS 2023), AppWorld (Trivedi et al., 2024), HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018), RULER.

CODE: none. The paper has formulas only. Eq. 12 selects segments with p >= tau (0.4) and takes the Top-K (K=5) per image. The cap is 20 segments per query.

FIGURES: The best single candidate is Figure 2, "Performance comparison under varying context token limits" (Text-RAG vs OCR-Memory at 1024, 2048, 4096 and 8192 tokens, four metrics, gains annotated). It shows the budget sensitivity at a glance. I did not extract it with figures.py. I know it only from the text layer, which has the axis labels and gains.

PROBLEMS: None of substance. The text layer has some garbled math and the Figure 1 text is jumbled. No embedded instructions were found. The appendix had no extra result tables, only hyperparameters (LoRA r=16, alpha=32, tau=0.4, K=5, lr 1e-5, batch 128, loss weights 2.0 and 1.0).
